prompt_title: Unified Viewport Shell — Standardize Layout, Sidebars, Controls, and Chrome Across All 3D Modules

section_A.title: YOUR RAW INSTRUCTION
section_A.content:
Our 3D Lab has 209 modules across 7 templates, but the viewport layout is inconsistent. Each template assembles its own sidebar/panel structure. DevControlsModule has its own panel system with custom minimize buttons, its own usePanelState hook, and its own BottomSheet for mobile. WallConfigurator has its own ConfigPanel and BOMPanel. The standard templates use a mix of GenericControlPanel, ControlPanel, InfoPanel, LabPanelLayout, and ComplianceReportPanel — none of which share a common container or collapse behavior. The floating toolbar with orbit/pan/perspective/isometric/reset controls only exists in DevControlsModule's CameraPresetBar. crossSectionEnabled and explodedViewEnabled are scaffolded in useLabViewStore but never wired to UI.

I need a Unified Viewport Shell specification — a slot-based layout system where:
1. The SHELL owns the containers: header bar, left sidebar slot, right sidebar slot, canvas area, floating toolbar, mobile bottom sheet.
2. The shell provides all CHROME: panel collapse/expand with a SINGLE minimize button component, panel headers, responsive breakpoints, scroll behavior.
3. TEMPLATES only inject CONTENT into named slots — they never create their own sidebar containers, collapse buttons, or panel wrappers.
4. Modules declare via config which slots they use (e.g., a simple exploded module might only use rightSidebar for parts legend; DevControls uses both sidebars).
5. A consistent floating toolbar with camera presets, view modes, toggles appears in ALL modules — config-driven to show/hide specific controls.
6. Mobile layout is handled by the shell: sidebars collapse to bottom sheet tabs automatically.
7. Adding a new module is pure plug-and-play: write a config, inject slot content, done.

This must be industry-grade architecture (slot pattern, composition over inheritance, config-driven) but startup-flexible (easy to add/remove/reorder slots without refactoring).

hard_constraints: DO NOT modify, replace, or rename the SLIDE TO SUBMIT / SLIDE TO START UI pattern (not part of 3D Lab, mentioned for boundary clarity)
DO NOT break the demand frameloop (frameloop='demand') — every scene-affecting control must call invalidate()
DO NOT add new npm dependencies without explicit justification — compose from drei, Three.js, Zustand, Shadcn UI, and existing SlateCamp primitives
DO NOT touch the 4 legacy bespoke scenes (FARPlayground, ClassicalOrders, NBCPEnvelope, DevControlsModule) in Phase 1 — they migrate in a later phase
DO NOT create per-template sidebar containers, collapse buttons, or panel wrappers — the shell provides ALL containers, templates inject CONTENT only
DO NOT render UI controls on mobile that require hover — all controls must be tap-friendly with 44×44px minimum touch targets
DO NOT introduce state that bypasses the existing Zustand architecture — extend existing stores or create focused new stores following the established pattern
PRESERVE all existing spec content verbatim — this is an UPDATE (EXTEND) operation

CAGE integration for in-canvas quiz is undecided — flag it, don't assume
crossSectionEnabled and explodedViewEnabled exist in useLabViewStore but are not wired to any UI or renderer — this spec must wire them

Whether the floating toolbar should be rendered inside R3F Canvas (via drei Html) or in the DOM — DOM preferred for performance
Whether FocusModeToggle merges into the shell toolbar or remains standalone

current_divergence_audit.description: This is the problem. Each template/module assembles its own viewport layout from a grab-bag of components. No shared container, no shared collapse behavior, no shared chrome.

shell_components_current.LabModuleShell: Thin layout wrapper — provides LabTopBar + content area. Does NOT enforce sidebar structure.
shell_components_current.LabViewportFrame: R3F Canvas host with WebGLErrorBoundary + DOMOverlayLayer. Layout-agnostic — just provides the canvas.
shell_components_current.LabMetaPanel: Metadata side panel — used by some templates, ignored by others.
shell_components_current.LabPanelLayout: Panel layout wrapper in templates/ — provides a panel container but has no collapse/expand behavior shared with other panels.

panel_implementations_divergent.GenericControlPanel: Used by standard parametric template for slider controls. Has its own styling and layout.
panel_implementations_divergent.ControlPanel: Separate parametric control panel — different from GenericControlPanel. Two implementations for the same purpose.
panel_implementations_divergent.InfoPanel: Template info panel — different container styling from ControlPanel.
panel_implementations_divergent.ComplianceReportPanel: Compliance summary panel — its own layout, used only in specific contexts.
panel_implementations_divergent.DevControlsModule_dashboard: 55+ file bespoke module with its own dashboard/ directory, custom panels, custom usePanelState hook, BottomSheet, MobileSheetContent, and a DIFFERENT minimize button component.
panel_implementations_divergent.WallConfigurator_ConfigPanel: Wall configurator's own config panel with 5-step wizard — its own container.
panel_implementations_divergent.WallConfigurator_BOMPanel: Bill of materials panel — its own container separate from ConfigPanel.

controls_inconsistency.camera_presets: CameraPresetBar ONLY exists in DevControlsModule. Standard templates have no camera preset UI — users can only orbit freely.
controls_inconsistency.view_modes: No perspective/orthographic/isometric switcher in any standard template. SceneConfig supports orthographic prop but no UI to toggle it.
controls_inconsistency.cross_section: crossSectionEnabled exists in useLabViewStore. No UI toggle. No clipping plane implementation wired to it.
controls_inconsistency.exploded_view: explodedViewEnabled exists in useLabViewStore. No UI toggle. Exploded template has its own slider but it's not connected to this store field.
controls_inconsistency.human_scale: HumanSilhouette component exists. showHumanScale exists in some configs. No universal toggle in UI.
controls_inconsistency.reset_camera: resetCamera action exists in useLabViewStore. No button in any standard template exposes it.
controls_inconsistency.focus_mode: FocusModeToggle exists as standalone component. Not part of any consistent toolbar.

current_divergence_audit.minimize_button_divergence: DevControlsModule has its own sidebar minimize/collapse button component (part of usePanelState). Standard templates using LabPanelLayout have a different collapse behavior (or none). The visual appearance and interaction of 'collapse this sidebar' is different depending on which module you're in.

block_4_required_document_structure.title: REQUIRED DOCUMENT STRUCTURE — Section 12A: Unified Viewport Shell
block_4_required_document_structure.description: Every subsection is mandatory. Use exact header names. This replaces the previous toolbar-only prompt with a full shell system.

content: What the Unified Viewport Shell is: a slot-based layout system that standardizes every viewport container and chrome element.

WHY it exists: the per-template layout audit (from PHASE_1) proves that N different panel containers, M different collapse buttons, and inconsistent controls create maintenance burden and UX inconsistency.
Governing principles:
(1) Slot-based composition: Shell provides containers, templates provide content.
(2) Config-driven layout: Modules declare which slots they use and which toolbar controls they need via ViewportShellConfig.
(3) Single source of chrome: ONE panel container component, ONE collapse button, ONE toolbar — shared by all 209 modules.
(4) Convention over configuration: Each template type has sensible defaults. Modules override only when needed.
(5) DOM-rendered chrome: All shell UI is outside the R3F Canvas for zero WebGL performance cost.
(6) Mobile-first: Sidebars collapse to bottom sheet tabs. Toolbar collapses to icon row.
(7) Demand-frameloop-safe: Scene-affecting controls call invalidate(). UI-only controls don't.
Include a BEFORE/AFTER table: for each template, show which components handle layout TODAY vs. the unified shell component they'll use.
Define the slot model. The shell provides these named layout regions:
- HEADER: Top bar with back nav, module title, and quick actions. Already exists as LabTopBar — absorb it.
- LEFT_SIDEBAR: Optional. Module info, navigation, metadata. Width: collapsible, default 280px.
- CANVAS: The R3F viewport. Always present. Fills remaining space.
- RIGHT_SIDEBAR: Primary controls — parametric sliders, layer toggles, part legends, config wizards. Width: collapsible, default 320px.
- TOOLBAR: Floating toolbar overlaying the canvas. Camera presets, view modes, toggles, reset.
- BOTTOM_SHEET (mobile only): Replaces both sidebars on < 768px. Tab-based: each sidebar becomes a tab.
- STATUS_BAR: Optional. Compliance summary, dimension readout, violation count. Anchored to bottom of canvas area.
Show an ASCII layout diagram for DESKTOP and MOBILE.
Define the TypeScript interface for slot content injection — templates pass React nodes to named slots.
CRITICAL: Templates NEVER render their own <div> wrappers for sidebars. They return slot content. The shell wraps it.
Define TWO interfaces that extend ModuleConfig:
1. ViewportShellConfig — declares which LAYOUT SLOTS the module uses:
- leftSidebar: boolean | { defaultCollapsed?: boolean, width?: number }
- rightSidebar: boolean | { defaultCollapsed?: boolean, width?: number }
- statusBar: boolean
- mobileBottomSheetTabs: string[] (tab labels for bottom sheet)
2. ViewportCapabilities — declares which TOOLBAR CONTROLS the module supports:
- cameraPresets: boolean | CameraPreset[] (custom presets)
- viewModes: Array<'perspective' | 'orthographic' | 'isometric' | 'top-down'>
- crossSection: boolean | { axis: 'x' | 'y' | 'z', range: [number, number] }
- explodedView: boolean
- humanScale: boolean
- focusMode: boolean
- resetCamera: boolean
- measurementTool: boolean (future)
Show how these merge into the ModuleConfig discriminated union.
Define DEFAULT values per template type (the convention-over-configuration layer).
Show a concrete example: a parametric module config WITH and WITHOUT explicit overrides.
🔄 ARCHITECTURE IMPACT: Modifies ModuleConfig type in types/templates.ts.
Define the complete component tree for the Unified Viewport Shell.
Root: ViewportShell — receives resolved config + slot content, renders the layout.
Children:
- ViewportHeader: Absorbs LabTopBar. Adds quick-action buttons from capabilities.
- ViewportSidebar: SINGLE sidebar container used for BOTH left and right. Props: side ('left' | 'right'), collapsed state, onCollapse, children (slot content). ONE minimize button component built in.
- ViewportCanvas: Wraps LabViewportFrame. No changes to Canvas internals.
- ViewportToolbar: Floating toolbar. Config-driven button groups.
- ViewportBottomSheet: Mobile only. Tab-based. Each tab = one sidebar's content.
- ViewportStatusBar: Optional. Compliance/dimension summary.
Show the Mermaid component tree.
Show WHERE ViewportShell mounts: it REPLACES LabModuleShell in the component hierarchy.
FOR EACH COMPONENT provide:
- File path: src/features/3d-lab/components/shell/{ComponentName}.tsx
- Props interface (TypeScript, extracted from codebase patterns)
- Zustand store dependencies
- Invalidation pattern (if it affects 3D scene)
- Mobile adaptation
- Which current component(s) it REPLACES or ABSORBS
🔄 ARCHITECTURE IMPACT: Replaces LabModuleShell. Absorbs LabTopBar, LabMetaPanel.

This is the KEY unification point. Currently there are 7+ different panel/container components (GenericControlPanel, ControlPanel, InfoPanel, LabPanelLayout, ComplianceReportPanel, DevControlsModule dashboard panels, WallConfigurator ConfigPanel). ALL of them get replaced by ONE shared ViewportSidebar component.
ViewportSidebar provides:
- Consistent panel header with title + subtitle
- ONE collapse/minimize button — same visual, same animation, same position in ALL modules
- Smooth collapse/expand animation (CSS transition, not JS)
- Scroll behavior for overflow content
- Section dividers between content groups (templates inject sections, shell renders dividers)
- Responsive: at < 768px, sidebar content moves to ViewportBottomSheet tab
Define the TypeScript interface for ViewportSidebar.
Define the SidebarSection sub-component — templates inject an array of SidebarSection elements.
Show a CONCRETE before/after: how ParametricScene currently renders GenericControlPanel vs. how it will inject content into ViewportSidebar.
Show a CONCRETE before/after: how DevControlsModule currently renders its custom panels vs. how it will inject content into ViewportSidebar slots.
The collapse/minimize button:
- Component: PanelCollapseButton (ONE component, used everywhere)
- Position: top-right corner of the sidebar panel header
- Icon: ChevronRight (collapse) / ChevronLeft (expand) for right sidebar, reversed for left
- Animation: sidebar width transitions from default to 0px (collapsed) with content fading
- State: managed by shell store, NOT by individual templates
- Keyboard: Ctrl+[ for left sidebar, Ctrl+] for right sidebar
The toolbar that was the original prompt scope — now properly nested within the shell.
Position: bottom-center of the canvas area, floating above content.
Structure: horizontal button group with icon buttons, separated into logical groups by thin dividers.
Button groups (all config-driven via ViewportCapabilities):
Group 1 — View Modes: Perspective | Orthographic | Isometric | Top-Down
Group 2 — Camera Presets: Front | Top | Iso | Close-Up | Wide (+ custom presets from config)
Group 3 — Scene Toggles: Cross-Section | Exploded View | Human Scale | Wireframe (future)
Group 4 — Actions: Reset Camera | Focus Mode | Screenshot (future)
Each button renders ONLY if the corresponding capability is enabled in config.
Active state: filled icon + subtle background. Inactive: outline icon.
Define the TypeScript interface for ViewportToolbar and ToolbarButton.
Define the camera preset system: CameraPreset interface, animated transitions, OrbitControls sync.
Define the cross-section toggle: wires crossSectionEnabled from useLabViewStore to a THREE.Plane clipping system.
Define the view mode switcher: how perspective/orthographic camera swap works with SceneConfig.
Show the invalidation flow for each button type.
Mobile (< 768px): toolbar becomes a compact icon row with overflow menu for less-used controls.
Decide: new focused store or extend useLabViewStore.

Recommendation: CREATE new useViewportShellStore for shell-specific state (sidebar collapsed, active view mode, active camera preset). KEEP useLabViewStore for scene-affecting toggles (crossSectionEnabled, explodedViewEnabled) since they're already there.
Define the FULL interface for useViewportShellStore:
- leftSidebarCollapsed: boolean
- rightSidebarCollapsed: boolean
- activeViewMode: 'perspective' | 'orthographic' | 'isometric' | 'top-down'
- activeCameraPreset: string | null
- mobileActiveTab: string (which bottom sheet tab is active)
- toolbarExpanded: boolean (mobile only — toolbar overflow state)
- Actions: toggleLeftSidebar, toggleRightSidebar, setViewMode, setCameraPreset, setMobileTab, etc.
Show the updated useLabViewStore interface with the wired fields.
Show the invalidation bridge: which store changes trigger invalidate() and which are UI-only.
Show how the existing useLabStore facade handles the new store (or if it needs updating).
🔄 ARCHITECTURE IMPACT: Store count increases from 10 to 11.

12A_8_template_integration_pattern.header: ### 12A.8 Template Integration Pattern — How Templates Plug Into the Shell
content: This is the plug-and-play contract. Define the EXACT pattern a template follows to use the shell.
Step 1: Template component receives its ModuleConfig (which now includes ViewportShellConfig + ViewportCapabilities with defaults applied).
Step 2: Template returns a ViewportShellContent object with named slot content:
- leftSidebarContent?: ReactNode (or array of SidebarSection)
- rightSidebarContent?: ReactNode (or array of SidebarSection)
- canvasContent: ReactNode (the R3F scene — this is what templates primarily provide)
- statusBarContent?: ReactNode
Step 3: The parent (ViewportShell or LabViewport) receives this content and injects it into the shell slots.
Show the TypeScript interface: ViewportShellContent.
Show a COMPLETE before/after refactor for ONE template (ParametricScene recommended — it's the most common with ~100 modules).
Show the pattern for a minimal module: just canvasContent, no sidebars (e.g., a simple animated sequence).
Show the pattern for a complex module: both sidebars + custom toolbar presets (e.g., DevControlsModule migration target).
CRITICAL: Templates must NEVER import ViewportSidebar, PanelCollapseButton, or ViewportToolbar directly. They only produce content. The shell renders the containers.
Table: for each of the 7 template types, show the DEFAULT shell configuration.
Columns: Template Type | Left Sidebar | Right Sidebar | Toolbar Groups | View Modes | Status Bar | Notes | Learning Rationale
Example defaults:
parametric: no left, yes right (control panel), all toolbar groups, perspective+isometric, status bar for violations, 'Sliders are the primary interaction — right sidebar is mandatory'
exploded: no left, yes right (parts legend), view modes + explode toggle, perspective+isometric, no status bar, 'Parts legend helps identify assembly layers'
floorplan: no left, yes right (room/path info), top-down + perspective only, orthographic default, status bar for egress metrics, 'Floor plans are inherently 2D — top-down default'
cutaway: no left, yes right (layer info), cross-section toggle mandatory, perspective+isometric, no status bar, 'Cross-section is the defining interaction'
animated: no left, yes right (step controls), camera presets + perspective, no status bar, 'Step controls drive the animation sequence'
calculator: no left, yes right (calculator inputs), minimal toolbar (reset only), orthographic, status bar for BOM, 'Calculators are 2D-focused tools'
wall-configurator: no left, yes right (5-step wizard), all toolbar groups, perspective+isometric, status bar for BOM, 'Wizard drives the entire interaction'
Module configs can OVERRIDE any of these defaults. Show override syntax.
Breakpoint: 768px (matches existing mobile detection in PerformanceMonitor).
Desktop → Mobile transformations:
- Left sidebar → hidden (content moves to bottom sheet 'Info' tab if leftSidebar was enabled)
- Right sidebar → bottom sheet primary tab (labeled by template: 'Controls', 'Layers', 'Parts', etc.)
- Floating toolbar → compact icon row pinned above bottom sheet. Max 5 icons visible, overflow in '...' menu.
- Status bar → collapsed to single-line summary above bottom sheet.
Bottom sheet behavior:
- Default height: 40% of viewport. Drag handle to resize (30% to 70% range).
- Tab bar at top: template defines tab labels via mobileBottomSheetTabs config.
- Scroll within each tab independently.
- Collapse fully with swipe-down gesture (canvas goes full screen).
- Re-expand with swipe-up from bottom edge or tap on tab bar.
All touch targets: 44×44px minimum.
No hover-dependent interactions.
Show the TypeScript interface for mobile-specific shell state.
⚠️ NEEDS PRODUCT INPUT: Should the bottom sheet use a native-feel drag gesture (like iOS sheets) or a simpler expand/collapse toggle?
The shell is 100% DOM-rendered — zero Three.js scene objects added.
Sidebar collapse/expand: CSS transition only. No React re-renders of Canvas.
Floating toolbar: static DOM. Button clicks dispatch store actions → store calls invalidate() only for scene-affecting changes.
Controls that don't affect the 3D scene (sidebar collapse, tab switch, info panel scroll) MUST NOT call invalidate().
Camera transitions: useFrame with useAnimationComplete — self-terminating.
Cross-section clipping plane: adds exactly 1 THREE.Plane to renderer.clippingPlanes (not scene graph).
Measurable targets:
- Toolbar render: < 2ms total paint time
- Sidebar collapse animation: 200ms CSS transition, 0 JS frames
- Shell total DOM nodes: < 80 (toolbar + both sidebars + header + status bar)
- Shell JS bundle: < 15KB gzipped (all shell components combined)
- Zero continuous useFrame loops from shell — only during animated camera transitions
- Mobile bottom sheet drag: 60fps (CSS transform, not layout)
5-phase migration from current divergent implementations to unified shell.
Phase 1 — Shell Foundation (LOW RISK):
Build ViewportShell, ViewportSidebar, PanelCollapseButton, ViewportToolbar (with reset camera only).
Ship ONLY to the 4 DASHBOARD_VISIBLE modules: stairway-configurator, calculator-flooring, unified-wall-configurator, site-development-controls.
Current implementations remain as fallback — shell is opt-in via feature flag.

Replace GenericControlPanel, ControlPanel, InfoPanel with ViewportSidebar slot injection.
Add camera presets + view mode switcher to toolbar.
Wire crossSectionEnabled for cutaway template.
Affected files: [list]
Phase 3 — Remaining Templates (MEDIUM RISK):
Migrate FloorPlanWalkthrough, AnimatedSequence, CalculatorTemplate.
Add human scale toggle. Wire explodedViewEnabled for exploded template.
Affected files: [list]
Phase 4 — WallConfigurator Migration (MEDIUM RISK):
Move ConfigPanel, BOMPanel content into ViewportSidebar slots.
5-step wizard becomes right sidebar content. BOM becomes status bar or second sidebar section.

Phase 5 — DevControlsModule Migration (HIGH RISK):

| Component | Replaced By | Remove After Phase |
| LabModuleShell | ViewportShell | Phase 2 |

12A_14_extensibility_pattern.header: ### 12A.14 Extensibility — Adding New Slots, Controls, or Panels
content: Adding a new TOOLBAR CONTROL (e.g., wireframe mode):
1. Add capability flag to ViewportCapabilities.
2. Add default to template defaults matrix.
3. Add store field (if scene-affecting: useLabViewStore, if UI-only: useViewportShellStore).
4. Create ToolbarButton entry in ViewportToolbar's config map.

NONE of these require modifying existing templates or modules — the shell absorbs new capabilities.
